edit.description: runFanout's per-entry setupWorktree hook call gets the same per-entry isolation createWorktree already has: a throw records a provisionFailure and parks that entry instead of rejecting the whole Promise.all

summary: Guard runFanout's per-entry setupWorktree hook so one entry's throw parks that entry instead of crashing the whole wave.

per.section: Every `.git/worktrees` mutation is serialized; the agent fanout is not

tests: a two-entry wave where one entry's setupWorktree hook throws still completes: the throwing entry is recorded in provisionFailures and stays pending, the other proceeds to runFanoutEntry
worktree/extraEnv indices stay aligned to the surviving entries after a sibling's hook failure is spliced out
acceptance: A setupWorktree hook throw on one entry of a multi-entry wave no longer crashes the tick; that entry is parked via provisionFailures exactly like a createWorktree failure, and siblings still ship.
notes: inbox 2026-08-03. chain.ts's setupBuildWorktree docstring (~L210-217) documents this gap as current fact; chain.ts is outside every phase lane, so updating that docstring once this ships is an operator follow-up, not part of this entry.

edit.description: add scopeWritesToEntry?: boolean (default false); correct entryChannelPaths doc to describe entry narrowing as opt-in, not automatic on every scoped tick
runAfterCommitGates passes the entry write-scope to writablePathsGate only when phase.scopeWritesToEntry is true; otherwise undefined, matching a singleton tick
prependHarnessBlock renders effectiveFenceLines only when phase.scopeWritesToEntry; otherwise unscopedFenceLines even with an assignedEntry

summary: Gate entry-scoped write narrowing behind Phase.scopeWritesToEntry (default false); dispatcher and prompt both respect it.

per.section: The entry-scoped write guard is opt-in, and off by default

tests: a scoped tick on a phase with scopeWritesToEntry undeclared writes with the same allowance and renders the same fence as a singleton tick (writablePaths ceiling only)
a scoped tick on a phase with scopeWritesToEntry: true narrows to entry.files ∪ entryChannelPaths under writablePaths and the prompt renders the two-fence block — unchanged from today's behavior
acceptance: Phase.scopeWritesToEntry (default false) governs both the write guard and the prompt fence identically; flume's own chain (which declares nothing) gets containment-only on every tick, scoped or not.
notes: Closes the two > **Drift:** notes in spec/pending.md and spec/prompt.md — one dispatcher ternary and one prompt fence choice, same mechanism. No .flume/chain.ts change needed; default false already matches flume's own expectation.

new.description: drives loadChainModule + buildFlumeApi against .flume/chain.ts to exercise the four predicates below

summary: Add behavioral test coverage for chain.ts's four load-bearing predicates: plan.shouldRun, plan.handoff, build.handoff, setupBuildWorktree.

per.section: Declining a tick before the invocation

tests: plan.shouldRun declines only when pending.json carries a pickable entry AND inbox.md is empty; runs on a non-empty inbox, a missing inbox.md, an empty queue, a parked-only queue, a live-blocked queue, a promotable-only queue, and undefined pending
plan.handoff's `Plan continues:` regex over state.md correctly drives re-wake vs handoff, including an absent line
build.handoff's wake condition, including the voluntary-bail leg
setupBuildWorktree's sentinel assertion throws when node_modules/<sentinel> is missing after install and passes when present
acceptance: The four predicates are driven through the real chain factory (loadChainModule + buildFlumeApi, as tests/examples.integration.test.ts already drives examples/), not a hand-copied reimplementation of chain.ts's logic.
notes: inbox 2026-08-02, narrowed to the four predicates only — chain.ts's declarations (writablePaths, gate lists, entry extension) are out of scope, same as CLAUDE.md itself. Declares tests/chain.test.ts to satisfy PENDING-ZERO-FILES-SCHEMA-FLOOR's new non-empty-files floor.

new.description: derive the [Unreleased] section from git log since the last release tag, per spec/cli.md Versioning policy

edit.description: add a script entry invoking the changelog tool

summary: Add a release-time tool that derives the [Unreleased] changelog section from git history since the last release tag.

per.section: Versioning policy

tests: derives [Unreleased] content from the commit range since the last release tag, using build: commit subjects as entry tags and bodies as the why
a tag history that stops short of CHANGELOG.md's latest recorded version (tags at v0.6.2, CHANGELOG at 0.9.0) resolves via a defined fallback, not an assumption
a zero-commit range refuses loudly instead of emitting an empty [Unreleased] section
preserves the ### Breaking subheading convention for commits whose body marks a break
acceptance: Running the tool over real history produces a well-formed [Unreleased] section per spec/cli.md Versioning policy, and it refuses non-zero on a zero-commit range.
notes: inbox 2026-08-03, successor to the reverted .changeset/ fragment approach (e87c007). Ships the tool only; running it at an actual release cut is separate.

edit.description: superviseLoop counts a non-zero child exit as an errored tick even when the child wrote no on-disk verdict

summary: A tick that dies without writing a verdict (throwing hook, CJS refusal, detached-HEAD refusal) is invisible to erroredTicks, so a run where nothing succeeded can exit 0.

per.section: Exit codes — the run never lies to CI

tests: a child exiting non-zero with no verdict written on disk is counted in the run's erroredTicks total
loopExitCode returns non-zero for a run where every tick refused before writing a verdict and nothing shipped
acceptance: superviseLoop increments erroredTicks for a non-zero child exit regardless of whether a tick verdict was written; loopExitCode reflects it.
notes: inbox 2026-08-03. A throwing chain hook also leaves the baton empty (sleep ran, handoff never reached), so a hibernating loop currently reports clean success over a run that errored.

edit.description: build and persist a tick verdict recording the wave's shipped tags before commitPendingUpdate's PendingParseFailure propagates out of tick()'s catch

summary: A wave that cherry-picks and gates N entries clean, then hits a PendingParseFailure on the ledger rewrite, writes no verdict at all — shipped tags never reach the run totals.

per.section: The tick verdict — one facts artifact

tests: a wave that cherry-picks and gates entries clean, then fails commitPendingUpdate's strict readPending, still writes a tick verdict recording the shipped tags
acceptance: A ledger-rewrite PendingParseFailure no longer discards a wave's verdict; the exit-69 refusal to write a corrupt ledger is unchanged, only the verdict loss is fixed.
notes: equilibrium audit, wave durability cluster. Exit code stays 69; only the missing verdict is the defect.

edit.description: tick command clears the previous tick-verdict.json before the detached-HEAD refusal returns, not after

summary: flume tick's detached-HEAD refusal returns above clearTickVerdict, so a loop with a detached HEAD mid-run re-reads the previous tick's stale verdict every iteration.

per.section: The tick verdict — one facts artifact

tests: flume tick against a detached HEAD clears tick-verdict.json before refusing, so a subsequent read finds no stale verdict
acceptance: The detached-HEAD refusal no longer leaves a prior tick's verdict on disk.
notes: equilibrium audit, exit-code contract cluster. A stale provisioning-failure signature on the old verdict can otherwise drive provisionFailureStreak toward abortThreshold spuriously.

edit.description: currentRefPath distinguishes a detached HEAD, a non-repository cwd, and a failing git invocation instead of returning null for all three
tick and loop branches print the message matching whichever of the three currentRefPath now reports

summary: currentRefPath returns null for three distinct states; both CLI call sites print "HEAD is detached" for all of them, so a caller outside a repo is told about a state it isn't in.

per.section: The loop lock and the tip claim

tests: currentRefPath distinguishes a detached HEAD from a non-repository cwd and from a git invocation failure
flume tick outside a git repository reports that, not "HEAD is detached"
acceptance: The three null-producing cases are distinguishable at the call site and the CLI prints the correct message for each.
notes: equilibrium audit, exit-code contract cluster.

edit.description: checkTipMoved / revertTipMovedCommit account for a tick that produced more than one commit, not just the newest
softReset call site passes the tick's actual commit count instead of the hardcoded 1

summary: An agent making two commits in one invocation trips checkTipMoved on parent-mismatch, and the soft-reset undoes only the newest — the first commit stays on the tip, un-gated.

per.section: Tip verify — commit only onto the tip the tick started on

tests: an agent that makes two commits in one tick invocation has both undone by the tip-moved revert, not just the newest
a single-commit tick's tip-moved revert behavior is unchanged
acceptance: A multi-commit agent invocation on a tip-moved tick is fully reverted; no un-gated commit is left on the tip.
notes: equilibrium audit, wave durability cluster. One-commit-per-tick is currently asserted only in prompt prose, not enforced — this closes the gap that assumption leaves.

edit.description: superviseLoop's consecutive-identical-failure backstop checks every signature in a tick's provisionFailures, not just index 0

summary: The abort backstop compares only provisionFailures[0]?.signature, so a repeated signature shadowed by a varying sibling at index 0 never accumulates a streak and never aborts.

per.section: Provisioning failures — quarantine, then abort

tests: a repeated provisioning-failure signature buried behind a varying sibling at provisionFailures[0] on every tick still accumulates the consecutive-failure streak and aborts at the threshold
acceptance: The backstop tracks every distinct signature across a tick's provisionFailures, not only the first.
notes: equilibrium audit, wave durability cluster. runFanout pushes a repo-level prune failure first, then per-entry failures — the untagged repo-level class is exactly what a tagged sibling at index 0 shadows today.

edit.description: require at least one declared path across files.new/files.edit/files.retire combined
cover the new floor

summary: An entry declaring empty files parses clean, is pickable, and can never be classified shipped — it commits real work every wave and never leaves the queue.

per.section: Ship detection requires a declared-files diff

tests: an entry whose files.new/edit/retire are all empty fails schema parse
an entry declaring at least one path in any of the three arrays still parses
acceptance: A zero-declared-files entry is rejected at parse instead of silently becoming unshippable forever.
notes: inbox 2026-08-03. Independent of the open SHIP-CLASSIFICATION-IS-THE-ENGINE-GUESSING question — proceeding per that finding's own recommendation. CHAINTS-PREDICATE-COVERAGE's files were amended this tick to stay valid under the new floor.

tests: flume job new against a CJS-context host exits 2 with the usage-shaped refusal as the headline message
acceptance: job new's CJS-context refusal matches tick's: exit 2, refusal headlined, not wrapped in the operational-failure message.

edit.description: the --job/FLUME_JOB resolution path refuses a name with no existing state root on every subcommand it reaches except job new; naming the job and the path it looked for; exit 2

flume --job nonexistent tick exits 2 and creates no directory
flume job new nonexistent still creates the state root
